name: Nitroweb Amazing Wishlist for WooCommerce
author: Nitroweb

sections.description:
Nitroweb Amazing Wishlist for WooCommerce gives your customers a wishlist with AJAX interactions.

Every customer gets one Wishlist that they can fill, share and shop from. Saved carts and admin reporting are available in a separate plugin from nitroweb.gr.

Free plugin documentation covers setup, shortcodes, sharing, alerts, and troubleshooting.

Core Wishlist Features

  • Add to Wishlist button on single product pages and shop/archive loops
  • Configurable button position: after Add to Cart, overlaid on the product image, icon-only, or fully manual placement
  • Customizable button text, icon (heart, bookmark, star, or none), and colours (text, border, background — including hover states)
  • Guest wishlist support via a browser cookie — no account required; merges into the user account on login
  • Wishlist page shortcode [nawfw_wishlist]
  • “Add all to cart” and “add selected to cart” bulk actions
  • Optional automatic removal of an item once it’s added to the cart
  • Sliding panel mini-widget showing the Wishlist count and contents
  • One-click Wishlist menu item in Appearance → Menus
  • Optional Wishlist link in the WooCommerce My Account menu
  • Sharing via a unique, unguessable link (the store owner can turn sharing off) and direct email sharing
  • Social sharing buttons: Facebook, X (Twitter), Pinterest, WhatsApp, Telegram
  • Show/hide price, stock status and date-added columns
  • “Wishlists” column on the WordPress Products list

Price-Drop & Back-in-Stock Alerts

  • Users set a target price per Wishlist item and are emailed automatically when it drops
  • Users opt in to a back-in-stock notification on any out-of-stock or backorder item
  • A twice-daily cron monitors prices; live WooCommerce hooks fire stock alerts instantly

Price-Drop Broadcast Notifications

  • Emails every registered user who has a product in their Wishlist whenever its price is reduced
  • Queued and throttled via WooCommerce Action Scheduler — configurable batch size and interval

Tools

  • Export / Import Settings — export the plugin’s configuration as a JSON file and import it on another site
  • 3rd-party Wishlist Importer — migrate from 16 other plugins with a live progress bar, no timeout risk, and automatic skipping of already-imported items. Supported sources: YITH WooCommerce Wishlist, TI WooCommerce Wishlist, Airy Wishlist, Saveto Wishlist, Smart Wishlist for More Convert (WLFMC), TH Wishlist, WCBoost Wishlist, WishSuite, WT WooCommerce Wishlist, JVM WooCommerce Wishlist, Premmerce WooCommerce Wishlist, ACO Wishlist, Qode Wishlist, Woo Smart Wishlist (WPClever), PickPlugins Wishlist, NM Gift Registry & Wishlist
  • Delete All Data on Uninstall — off by default; when enabled, uninstalling removes the plugin-created Wishlist page, custom tables, and settings

Under the Hood

  • Full AJAX interactions — no page reloads
  • WPML and Polylang compatible; Wishlist page auto-created for every active language
  • WooCommerce HPOS compatible
  • Theme-overridable templates (place them in your-theme/nitroweb-amazing-wishlist/)
  • Gutenberg block and Elementor widget for the Wishlist page and Add to Wishlist button
  • No bundled third-party libraries — only WordPress’s own jQuery
  • Translation-ready through WordPress.org language packs
sections.installation:
1. Upload the nitroweb-amazing-wishlist-for-woocommerce folder to /wp-content/plugins/
  2. Activate the plugin through the Plugins screen in WordPress
  3. Navigate to WooCommerce → Wishlist to configure

The plugin automatically creates a Wishlist page ([nawfw_wishlist]) on first activation. WooCommerce must be installed and active.

Upgrading from another wishlist plugin? Go to WooCommerce → Wishlist → Import — the plugin will detect which source plugins have data on your site and guide you through a one-click migration.
sections.faq:
Does it work for guests?

Yes. Guests get a wishlist stored in a browser cookie. It merges into their user account automatically when they log in or register.

Is it compatible with WPML and Polylang?

Yes. With WPML or Polylang active, the Wishlist page is automatically created and linked as a translation for every active language on activation.

Can I customise the templates?

Yes. Copy any template from the plugin’s templates/ folder to your-theme/nitroweb-amazing-wishlist/ and edit it freely — your file takes precedence.

Is the import safe to run on a live site?

Yes. Items that already exist in Amazing Wishlist are silently skipped (the database UNIQUE constraint is used), so the importer is idempotent and will not create duplicates even if run more than once.

How does the import progress bar work?

The import runs as a series of small AJAX batch requests (50 items per batch). The progress bar fills as batches complete. The page warns you not to close the tab while it runs, and the browser’s native close-tab warning fires too if you try.

Will importing delete data from the source plugin?

No. The importer only reads from the source plugin’s tables — it never modifies or deletes them. You can keep the old plugin active while you verify the migration, then deactivate it when you’re satisfied.

How do price-drop alerts work?

A twice-daily WP-Cron job compares the current price of each wishlisted product against the target price the user set. If the current price is at or below the target, an email is sent and the alert is cleared. Back-in-stock alerts are triggered by the woocommerce_product_set_stock_status hook and fire immediately when a product moves from out-of-stock or backorder to in-stock.
sections.changelog:
1.7.3

  • Escape wishlist buttons, icons, product images, and prices when rendering.
  • Use WordPress.org language packs for directory releases.

1.7.2 — 12 Nov 2026

  • Change: The database now stores exactly one wishlist per customer (unique per user and per guest session), with no list name or privacy fields.
  • Change: Sharing is controlled only by the “Enable Sharing” setting.

1.7.1 — 11 Nov 2026

  • Change: One wishlist per customer by design; the importer merges all of a customer’s source lists into it.
  • Change: All functions, classes, options, hooks, shortcodes, tables and files now use the unique nawfw prefix. Shortcodes are now [nawfw_wishlist] and [nawfw_mini_wishlist]; theme overrides go in your-theme/nitroweb-amazing-wishlist/.
  • Fix: Wishlist sharing now works and is controlled by the “Enable Sharing” setting.
  • Removed: Admin tabs that only showed upgrade notices.

1.7.0 — 04 Jul 2026

  • Feature: New Import settings tab — one-click wishlist migration from 16 popular plugins. Auto-detects which sources have data on the current site. Runs in batched AJAX (no timeouts), shows a live progress bar, reports imported vs. skipped counts, and is safe to re-run.

1.6.0 — 28 Jun 2026

  • Feature: Tools tab — export/import the plugin’s full configuration as a JSON file; a “Delete All Data on Uninstall” toggle (off by default) that when enabled removes all custom tables and settings on deletion.

1.5.0 — 28 Jun 2026

  • Feature: Setting to show/hide the icon on the Wishlist Appearance → Menus link.

1.3.0 — 05 Jun 2026

  • Feature: Price-drop alerts — per-item target price, emailed automatically on price reduction.
  • Feature: Back-in-stock alerts — opt-in notification when an out-of-stock wishlist item is restocked.
  • Feature: Price-drop broadcast notifications — email every wishlist watcher on any price reduction, queued and throttled via Action Scheduler.
  • Feature: Wishlist link in the WooCommerce My Account menu.
  • Feature: One-click Wishlist menu item in Appearance → Menus.
  • Feature: Wishlists column on the WordPress Products list.
  • Feature: Button colour settings and icon-only loop display.
  • Fix: corrected the “Add to Wishlist” toast text shown when removing an item.
  • Fix: resolved a double menu-item-creation bug on Appearance → Menus.
  • Fix: corrected a malformed cart icon in the sliding wishlist panel.

1.0.0 — 24 May 2026

  • Initial release.
